text:
maria_acme: Hey team — acme's production org in São Paulo (project:sao_prod) hit 429s last night ~22:03 BRT. Our monthly credits dropped to 0 then partially refilled around 01:10 BRT. We had a manual burst top-up at 21:45 local. Sample req ids: req_abc123, req_def456. Can someone check why the refill window looked shifted and why we got double-draws during retries?

ana-cs: Thanks, grabbing details. Can you paste org/project IDs, the exact UTC timestamps you observed, and any response headers from the 429s? If you have a curl snippet that repros, that helps a lot.

maria_acme: org: org-acme-42, proj: sao_prod
UTC times: 2026-02-28T23:03:12Z (first 429) -> 2026-03-01T04:10:20Z (first successful refill visible in UI)
Response headers we captured:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z
X-Request-ID: req_abc123
```
We uploaded full logs to ticket #12345 (linked).

carmen: fyi the monthly refill job runs at 00:00 UTC (server-side). Local time differences expected, but the partial-delayed restore and the correlation with a burst top-up is suspicious. tagging @raj @lee to investigate. :mag:

support-bot: monthly-refill-job executed 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z (duration: 12s) — processed 18,234 tenant buckets.

raj: looking into it. Two things to check quickly: (1) top-up flow can create a temporary "burst" bucket that should merge at cutover — if merge logic skipped that tenant it may show zero then partial later; (2) long-running streaming/batch requests that reconnect without idempotency can be double-counted on retries. Does your client set an Idempotency-Key for streaming uploads?

maria_acme: our ingestion client retries streaming uploads on socket close, and we do NOT set Idempotency-Key when using the streaming protocol. We relied on transport-level reconnects.

lee: I can repro a similar pattern locally. Quick repro steps: run a streaming batch that sends ~500k tokens across >1 hour, force a socket drop, then retry without Idempotency-Key. Example (very simplified):
```bash
# reproduce (unix shell)
for i in 1 2 3; do \
  curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @batch.json || true; \
done
```
You will see token counters increment for each retry attempt because the server treats each stream as a new consumption when no idempotency metadata is provided.

carmen: thanks. So root cause looks like a combo: burst top-up created separate accounting entry + streaming retries got counted multiple times. At midnight UTC our refill job merged many buckets, but the merge happened after some long-running retries continued to consume from the old temporary bucket, creating an apparent early depletion and a delayed partial refill.

raj: plan of action:
- Short term: issue goodwill credit to compensate the extra draw and update support note.
- Medium: add server-side dedupe for streaming reconnects that lack explicit Idempotency-Key (safety net).
- Docs: add client guidance to set Idempotency-Key for long uploads and reduce single-request token size.
- Ticket: INF-2026-432 created to track the merge timing edge-case and streaming dedupe work.

carmen: support — can you apply and confirm a credit?

ana-cs: applied 15,000 token goodwill credit to org-acme-42 at 2026-03-01T15:20:00Z and added note to ticket #12345. Please confirm visibility on your end. :white_check_mark:

maria_acme: Confirmed — the 15k tokens show up in the console now. Thank you! :pray:

lee: patch to dedupe-sidecar merged to staging, will be in the next deploy window (~6h). Also writing a small migration to ensure burst-topup buckets are merged atomically at cutover.

raj: follow-up items assigned in INF-2026-432: (a) harden merge ordering, (b) server-side reconnect dedupe, (c) client docs update. We'll keep this thread open for one week of validation.

carmen: closing the immediate support loop. If you see any further unexpected zeroes around cutover, ping this thread and we'll rerun the audit. Thanks for reporting and the repro details — that sped us up. :rocket:
